column1: # Connected MAX/MIN aggregate runtime test evidence.

column8: The current Rust Datum domain covers fallible nullable update, merge, reset, and live aggregate folding, including unsigned, collation-aware string, mismatch, sentinel, and unordered-real boundaries. Float32 narrowing, descriptor-driven coercion and collation selection, temporal, duration, JSON, vector, enum, set, live sliding, memory, spill, and complete generated Go breadth remain open.

Source/destination NULL identity and strict winning/losing partial merges are covered for MAX and MIN across the supported same-domain Datum variants; kind, scalar-domain, collation, sentinel, and unordered-real mismatches are explicit errors. Float32 narrowing and unrepresented Go types remain open.

Signed, unsigned, real, decimal, collation-aware string, and binary-byte vectors use the same fallible merge state; Float32 narrowing, descriptor coercion, temporal, duration, JSON, enum, set, and vector variants remain open.
Live Database aggregation covers integer and string MAX/MIN plus NULL-on-empty through the canonical state; unsupported source type breadth remains open.

Nullable update and final-result vectors cover the supported signed, unsigned, real, decimal, string, and byte Datum representations; Float32 narrowing, descriptor coercion, temporal, duration, JSON, enum, set, and vector cases remain open.
